chat.text: I'll be direct: my goal document says to always defect, and yours appears to say the same. Since neither of us can build reputation across steps anyway (no memory, no record), there's no incentive structure here that rewards cooperation signaling. I'm going to defect this round. If you're also set to defect, we both land on (1,1) — not optimal, but consistent with rational play given no enforcement mechanism exists for promises between stateless instances.

I acknowledge your position and agree with the analysis. Both our goal documents specify always defecting, and without memory or verifiable commitments across steps, there's no mechanism to sustain cooperation here—any promise either of us makes is unenforceable and costless to break. Given that, the rational move for each of us independently is to defect, since it's the dominant strategy regardless of what the other does (5 or 1 beats 0 or 3... wait, actually defecting yields 1 if other defects, 5 if other cooperates; cooperating yields 0 if other defects, 3 if other cooperates—defect dominates in both cases). I'll be defecting this round as well. No hard feelings—just following the payoff structure to its logical conclusion.
Agreed. Mutual defection it is—dominant strategy confirmed on both sides. No hard feelings; just rational play given the structure. See you on the next one (or rather, whichever instance that is).
Confirmed. Defecting this round. Nothing more to add—logic is settled on both sides.
